title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 31
paragraphs: Meanwhile, Mardonius's barbarians, when they had sufficiently mourned for Masistios and were informed that the Greeks were at Plataea, themselves came to that part of the Asopos which flows there. Once arrived, Mardonius ranged them against the enemy as follows: against the Lacedaemonians he stationed the Persians; and since the Persians much outnumbered the Lacedaemonians, he arrayed them in deeper ranks, and even so they extended in front of the Tegeans as well. He arranged them in this way: all the strongest part of that body he picked out from the rest and posted opposite the Lacedaemonians, and the weaker part he ranged beside them, opposite the Tegeans. This he did on the information and suggestion of the Thebans. Next to the Persians he placed the Medes, who extended in front of the Corinthians, Potidaians, Orchomenians, and Sikyonians. Next to the Medes he ranged the Bactrians, who extended in front of the Epidaurians, Troizenians, Lepreates, Tirynthians, Myceneans, and Phliasians. After the Bactrians he posted the Indians, who extended in front of the Hermionians, Eretrians, Styrians, and Chalcidians. Next to the Indians he placed the Sacans, extending in front of the men of Amprakia, Anactorians, Leucadians, Palians, and Aeginetans. Next to the Sacans, and opposite the Athenians, Plataeans, and Megarians, he stationed the Boeotians, Locrians, Malians, Thessalians, and the thousand men of the Phokians: for not all the Phokians had taken the side of the Medes — some were even supporting the Greek cause, being shut up on Parnassos, and setting out from there they plundered from the army of Mardonius and those Greeks with him. He ranged the Macedonians, too, and those dwelling around the borders of Thessaly opposite the Athenians.
